key_insight: Applying classical supervised ML models (KNN, LDA, QDA, Gaussian Process) to routine patient health data can improve early dementia prediction; explicitly addressing class imbalance noticeably improves model reliability.
problem_solved: The study tackles early and accurate dementia detection from clinical/health data, overcoming challenges of subtle predictive signals and class imbalance that degrade classifier performance in practice.
method: Train and compare supervised classifiers: K-Nearest Neighbors, Linear Discriminant Analysis, Quadratic Discriminant Analysis, and Gaussian Process Classifiers.
Preprocess clinical data and mitigate class imbalance using techniques such as resampling or class weighting to improve sensitivity to minority (dementia) cases.
Evaluate and compare models using standard classification metrics to identify reliable approaches for clinical screening.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a pragmatic comparison of classical classifiers on healthcare data and underscores the importance of imbalance-handling for trustworthy dementia screening models, guiding model choice for deployment in clinical pipelines.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing model performance (accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity) across KNN, LDA, QDA, and Gaussian Process
ROC curves and paired confusion matrices to highlight trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity
Pipeline diagram showing data flow: raw patient data → preprocessing → imbalance correction → model training → evaluation
Feature-contribution/coefficient plot or risk-score heatmap to show which clinical variables drive predictions
paper_title: Predictive Analytics for Dementia: Machine Learning on Healthcare Data
paper_authors: Shafiul Ajam Opee, Nafiz Fahad, Anik Sen, Rasel Ahmed, Fariha Jahan
